```{r,echo=FALSE}
# sqrt(ax) = b

while(T){
    sab = sample(c(-1,1),1)
    multer = sample(2:10,1)
    a = sample(2:6,1)*sab
    b = a*multer
    x = (b/a)^2
    if(x%%1==0 && abs(a)!=abs(b)){break}
}
eq = paste0(a,"\\sqrt{x}=",b)
eq2 = paste0("\\sqrt{x}=",multer)

eq3 = paste0(a,"\\sqrt{",x,"}\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)

eq4 = paste0(a,"\\cdot ",multer,"\\stackrel{?}{=}",b)
eq4 = gsub("+-","-",eq4,fixed=T)

```

Question
========

Solve.

$$`r eq`$$

Solution
========

Divide both sides by `r a`.


$$`r eq2`$$

Square both sides.

$$x=`r x`$$

Check the solution in the original equation.

$$`r eq3`$$

$$`r eq4`$$

Yup, that is true. So $x=`r x`$ is a solution to the given equation.
